explicit_validation.explanation: Paper validates LLM-generated rewrites against human judgments through multiple stages: measuring annotator agreement on original vs rewritten claims, human preference testing, and explanation point evaluation

prompts.notes: Full prompts provided in Appendix A.2, including subjectivity-focused prompts and prompts targeting specific ambiguity types (wording, minor assumptions, causation, interpretation)

inter_annotator_agreement.interpretation: Reports percentage of claims where all three annotators assign same faithfulness label

guidelines.notes: Appendix Figures 5 and 6 show study interfaces with evaluation instructions; annotators judged faithfulness, preference between original/rewritten claims, and importance of explanation points

sample_size.notes: Uses StorySumm dataset with 568 claims total; validation studies use subsets but exact sizes not specified

quantitative_scores.notes: Rewrites show statistically significant gains in annotator agreement compared to original claims
77% of rewrites preferred over original claims by human judges
68.72% of explanation points labeled IMPORTANT by majority vote

validation_results.summary_finding: LLM-generated rewrites significantly improve annotator agreement (21% absolute improvement) and are preferred by humans 77% of the time, with explanation points mostly rated as important (69%) and rarely wrong (<1%)

criteria_mapping.notes: LLM uses quantitative rewrite metrics while humans provide qualitative judgments, but both evaluate core aspects of claim subjectivity and faithfulness
